mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Registration Particulars)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: court-issued certificate presented to the Consular Authentication Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to receive apostille for use in any Apostille Convention state. Consular Legalization route for non-member states: same certificate, then MOFA legalization, then consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate in the destination state. The routes are parallel and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Tax Payment and Business Registration Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (District Tax Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: National Tax Service certificate authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section for Apostille Convention destinations. Consular Legalization route: NTS certificate followed by MOFA legalization and destination-state consular legalization. The applicant must select one route only, according to the destination state's treaty status.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation, Banking and Closing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder and Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public authorized under the Notary Public Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarized resolution and power of attorney submitted to MOFA for apostille. Consular Legalization route: notarization, MOFA legalization, then consular legalization by the destination country's Korean consular office. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (as filed and deposited with the Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa board and shareholders; certified copy from District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: registered Articles excerpted by the Court Registry, then MOFA apostille. Consular Legalization route: certified registry copy, MOFA legalization, then consular legalization in the foreign state. No sequence may include both apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean licensed bank evidencing account relationship and good conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank regulated by the Financial Services Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: original bank letter signed by authorized bank officer, bank seal authenticated, then MOFA apostille. Consular Legalization route: bank letter authenticated at bank headquarters, MOFA legalization, then destination-state consular legalization. Only one authentication path applies per destination state.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, shareholders, and counterparties of the KR Chusik Hoesa SPV must undergo mandatory enhanced due diligence screening against the KoFIU system, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the EU Consolidated Restrictive Measures List, and the Republic of Korea's domestic restrictions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Restriction on Financial Transactions for International Anti-Terrorism. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons must be treated as high risk, with source of wealth and source of funds independently verified and escalated to senior management approval. Screening includes fuzzy name matching, ID and passport verification, address verification, full ownership chain analysis, and adverse media checks. Transactions of any sanctioned person or jurisdiction are prohibited, and any hit must be reported to KoFIU under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act. The UBO is the natural person holding more than 25% of shares or exercising effective control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (Commercial Registration Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be rendered in the Korean alphabet as Hangul. A parallel English trade name may be used for bank and commercial purposes, but it must be a faithful transliteration or approved equivalent of the Hangul legal name. The suffix Chusik Hoesa or Stock Corporation must be included. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) legal form marker, (2) distinctive business core, (3) activity descriptor, and (4) optional group or territorial designator. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and foreign scripts are not permitted in the registered legal name unless transliterated into Hangul. Foreign-script company documents must match the registered transliteration exactly.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: tactical or official state symbols requiring prior approval by the Financial Services Commission, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Health and Welfare, or the relevant Central Administrative Agency
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a written appeal with the district court registrar within one month after the rejection, annexing the rejection notice, the proposed name, the desired registration details, and a memorandum demonstrating compliance with the Commercial Act's trade-name and public-order rules. The registrar will conduct de novo review and issue a written order. If the objection remains denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure in the court that supervises the registry. Alternatively, counsel may refile immediately with a revised name while preserving any right to appeal. The appeal must clearly distinguish the proposed name from all prior registered names and licensed sensitive tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable for a KR private equity buyout SPV. The National Tax Service requires a real physical place of business for corporate tax registration and VAT purposes, and Korean banks performing medium-risk enhanced due diligence for an SPV will reject a postal box address because they require on-site verification and a documented service agreement. A serviced office with a dedicated work station, meeting room access, signage, and a named company contact may be accepted if NTS and bank verification confirms the arrangement. The office must be capable of receiving official correspondence, board inspections, and regulatory notices.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: valid lease or service-level agreement in the SPV's name; physical signage; utility invoices; corporate books and board minutes maintained at the address; evidence of business activity, staffing, or professional officer availability; correspondence deliverability; NTS VAT filing consistency; bank statement and registered office matching. Quantified risk: approximately 55% or higher within 24 months for a purely virtual mailbox; approximately 25% for a professional serviced office with complete service-level agreements and physical attendance; approximately 10% for a wholly dedicated office with part-time officers, maintained records, and accurate tax filings. Unannounced inspection by NTS or municipal registry is legally permitted and increased for enhanced-risk SPVs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as consolidated and amended), particularly Articles 289, 291, 295, 300, 303, 317 and 332 for stock company formation; Articles 382 through 408 for directors, representative director and statutory auditor; Article 329 as amended to abolish any statutory minimum paid-up capital; Local Tax Act Articles and Corporate Registration Rules of the Supreme Court for filing mechanics.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Civil Registration Office of the competent District Court (Court Registry / Deungsogi) for the judicial district in which the SPV's registered office is located, operating through the Korean Court i-REG electronic filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (new-entity registration application) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting certificates, filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the amended Commercial Act. The subscribed shares must be fully paid in before incorporation registration, and the deposit certificate of a Korean financial institution must evidence the paid-in amount. The minimum par value is KRW 100 per share, so the theoretical minimum is KRW 100 if only one share is issued, but Korean banks and registry practice generally expect a de minimis operating capital deposit of at least KRW 1,000,000. The official state filing fee is not fixed; the court registry will assess registration tax based on actual capital and provide a bill at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the first formal decision of the board of directors of [Company Name], a Chusik Hoesa organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, that: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Payment. The board confirms the subscription statement and allotment schedule for the initially issued shares, and confirms that all such shares have been lawfully subscribed and that the full subscription price has been paid into a corporate capital deposit account maintained with a licensed Korean financial institution. The board approves the issuance of [NUMBER] shares with a par value of KRW [PAR VALUE] at an issue price of KRW [ISSUE PRICE] per share. The board ratifies the capital base as recorded in the deposit certificate and directs that it be included in the incorporation registration filing. 2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Corporation is adopted and fixed at [STREET ADDRESS, CITY, REPUBLIC OF KOREA]. The representative director is authorized to execute a lease for such office, to register such address with the competent District Court Registry, to register the corporate seal, and to take all ancillary actions. 3. Bank Accounts and Payment Rails. The Corporation authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts and the activation of SWIFT and syndicated wire payment rails with [BANK NAME], including foreign exchange settlement accounts necessary for the intended leveraged buyout acquisition syndicate. The board appoints [REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR NAME] as the primary authorized signatory and [SECOND DIRECTOR NAME] as the joint or secondary signatory. All transactions above USD 1,000,000 or equivalent require dual authorization unless otherwise mandated by the financing agreements. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The board unanimously appoints [REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR NAME] as Representative Director, [SECOND DIRECTOR NAME] as Executive Director, and [AUDITOR NAME] as Statutory Auditor of the Corporation. The auditor shall exercise independent oversight under the Commercial Act. The board authorizes the appointment of a company secretary, if required, for the maintenance of corporate records, board minutes, and regulatory filings. 5. Further Authorized Actions. The representative director is directed to complete the incorporation registration with the competent District Court Registry, to obtain the corporate seal certificate, to file business registration with the National Tax Service, to open all bank accounts, and to make any foreign investment report required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. 6. Effectiveness. All resolutions are immediately effective and any earlier oral or written instructions inconsistent herewith are superseded. The board orders the minutes of this meeting to be filed in the corporate seal and minutes book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Korean Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed notary public and the law firm acting as local counsel; notarization office recognized by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, including the corporate name, passive private equity SPV purposes aligned with ISIC 6499, authorized share capital, initial issued shares, registered office address, method of appointing directors, and auditor provisions. The purpose clause must be drafted narrowly to avoid inadvertently triggering the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act licensing requirements. Present the executed documents to a notary public for signature verification of all promoters and nominees. If a founder is outside Korea, execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of Korean counsel. Obtain a certified notation proving the notarized signatures before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation executed by all promoters
Notarized passports or identity cards of promoters and director nominees
Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney for any foreign promoter not present in Korea
Written consent to serve as director and statutory auditor
Intended registered office address confirmation
Authorized share capital breakdown and subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or local counsel raises any concern that the purpose clause resembles a regulated financial investment business, amend the purpose clause to state passive holding, acquisition, and investment activities only, provide a legal opinion on the exemption, and resubmit for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Subscribed Capital and Issuance of Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank or foreign exchange bank designated to accept the capital deposit; Foreign Exchange Information System portal if foreign funds are received
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital deposit passbook in the name of the future corporation, with the promoter or the newly formed board as the deposit controller. Remit 100% of the subscription price from the founders or, in a leveraged buyout, from permitted conduit funds into this account. Instruct the bank to issue a certificate of payment or a passbook evidencing the full deposit, as this document is mandatory for incorporation registration. Ensure that the movement of inbound foreign currency is reported to the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and if foreign ownership reaches the statutory threshold, file a foreign investment report with the bank or KOTRA. Protect the deposit by not withdrawing any funds until the incorporation registration is accepted.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation from Step 1
Subscribed share schedule and payment instructions
Provisional bank account opening form for the under-formation corporation
Identification and source of funds documentation for all subscribers
Proof of foreign remittance and exchange report for any non-resident subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open a provisional account before incorporation, use a Korean law-firm fiduciary or notarial escrow account to receive the capital, obtain a payment certificate from the financial institution, and transfer into the corporate bank account immediately after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office of the judicial district where the SPV's registered office is located, or the Korean Court i-REG electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the incorporation registration application Form and attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank payment certificate, officers' appointment documents, signature specimens, corporate seal registration statement, and any required resolutions. File the package electronically through i-REG or physically at the court registry counter. Pay the court registration tax assessed on the actual capital and any registry surcharges. The company is deemed incorporated only when the court accepts the registration. After acceptance, request the certified corporate registration certificate (registered matters certificate) and corporate seal certificate from the same registry.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration in the prescribed Korean form
Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate or passbook evidencing full payment of subscribed shares
Notarized minutes of the incorporation or promoters' meeting
Appointment acceptance by representative director, directors, and auditor
Corporate seal registration application and seal specimen
Evidence of registered office address and lease if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary instruction or suspends the filing, cure the stated deficiency, such as clarifying a foreign signature, providing a translation, or supplying a missing officer consent, within the court's correction period. If the rejection becomes final, appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure or refile after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Account Setup with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the Home Tax System (hometax.go.kr) and the local district tax office for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the court grants incorporation registration, file business registration with the National Tax Service to obtain a business registration number. Indicate the corporate tax class, the passive investment holding and buyout SPV nature, and the registered office address. If the company has no taxable turnover, still file the registration and file zero-return VAT declarations as required. Submit corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, representative director identification, lease agreement, and officer details. Upon acceptance, receive the business registration certificate and tax corporate account number. This step is mandatory for opening active bank accounts and for later corporate tax filings.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate from the District Court Registry
Corporate seal certificate
Identification of the representative director
Registered office lease agreement or legal right to use office
Bank certificate from the capital deposit account
Ultimate beneficial ownership chart if requested by the tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the lack of active revenue, submit an explanatory attestation that the SPV is a passive buyout vehicle and will file zero VAT and applicable corporate tax on investment income. Respond to any tax office notice within the stated deadline and request a written confirmation once the registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening, SWIFT/Syndicated Wire Setup, and Enhanced AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch with foreign exchange dealing authorization and the Financial Intelligence Unit reporting framework under the Financial Transactions Reports Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation registration certificate and corporate seal certificate to the chosen commercial bank. Submit the board resolution authorizing bank account opening and appointing signatories. Provide the bank complete beneficial ownership and source-of-wealth documentation because the private equity buyout SPV is classified as Medium Risk Enhanced. Configure SWIFT payment rails for syndicated loan wire transfers, including IBAN-equivalent Korean bank code, SWIFT/BIC, and account designations. Enter into the bank's AML/KYC agreement and obtain internet banking credentials with dual authorization. If the SPV enters into any foreign exchange transaction, file the appropriate transaction report through the bank. Ensure that the account mandate matches the board resolution exactly, including joint-signatory thresholds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate and company register excerpt
Board resolution authorizing the account opening
Passports of signatories and representative director
Ultimate beneficial ownership statement and corporate structure chart
Anti-money laundering and KYC questionnaire
Advised source of funds for the acquisition syndicate
SWIFT and wire transfer instruction form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's compliance department requires enhanced due diligence, provide a Korean counsel legal opinion explaining the passive SPV structure, the exemption from FSC licensing, the deal source and purpose, and the group's organizational chart. Escalate to the bank's AML review committee and establish a restricted account mandate if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory Notifications, Foreign Investment Reporting, and File Retention
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or designated foreign exchange bank for foreign investment reports; Korea Fair Trade Commission if merger clearance thresholds apply
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SPV has non-resident equity holders owning at least 10% of voting equity or controlling influence, file a report of foreign investment through KOTRA or a designated bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or within twenty days of the actual investment. If the leveraged buyout transaction targets a company and meets the statutory asset or revenue thresholds under the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, consult the Korea Fair Trade Commission on merger filing obligations. Preserve all board resolutions, signature specimens, bank confirmations, and foreign exchange reports in the corporate file. Obtain a Legal Entity Identifier if the financing agreement requires one. This step completes the statutory formation and governance groundwork.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form if foreign ownership threshold is met
Ultimate beneficial ownership chart
Subscription and payment evidence from the bank
Target company information if merger filing thresholds apply
Board resolution package including the pro-forma first board resolution
Corporate registration extracts and certificates obtained during prior steps
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a foreign investment filing is late, make a voluntary self-correction filing and pay any administrative surcharge. If a KFTC notification is required, file before consummation of the transaction or within the statutory period, and retain a legal opinion on the exemption or disclosure obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the SPV has no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing operation. If the company later establishes a physical facility, the competent authority would be the industrial licensing division of the relevant Metropolitan City or Provincial government and the Ministry of Environment through local environmental offices.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - passive private equity buyout SPV under ISIC 6499 and NAICS 525910 requires no industrial or manufacturing operating permit. No license is required under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act because the company will not engage in financial investment or lending activities requiring an FSC/FSS license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the relevant municipal environmental department would only have jurisdiction if a physical facility were to be constructed or operated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no construction, no stationary emission source, no wastewater discharge, no waste generation, and no physical industrial plant. This SPV does not trigger any Environmental Impact Assessment report, Environmental Registration, or pollution permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation in the corporate office model. If a future facility is added, it must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act, the Clean Air Conservation Act (VOC limits per stack and mg/m3 thresholds), and the Wastes Control Act for hazardous waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a passive paper SPV occupying only a leased office. If the entity uses physical office space, the building must maintain fire safety completion certificates, and the lessee must ensure compliance with the Fire Services Act and the Occupational Safety and Health Act to obtain civil defense and workplace safety clearance from the local fire department and the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: NTS HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa, complete commercial registration at the competent district court or the Supreme Court electronic registration system under the Commercial Act to obtain the corporate registration number. Then, within 20 days after business commencement, file a Business Registration Application through the NTS HomeTax portal with the competent district tax office. The application must include the articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, lease contract proving the domestic place of business, identity documents of the representative, and, for foreign investors, the foreign investment report certificate and investment registration certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Upon approval, the NTS assigns the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the VAT and corporate income tax identifier and must be used on all tax invoices and filings. A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business is not obliged to obtain a local BRN solely for offshore activities; however, if it becomes liable to Korean VAT or wishes to claim treaty benefits or input VAT refunds, it must register via HomeTax as a foreign corporation through a Korean domestic tax representative, submitting the foreign entity's registration certificate, articles or equivalent constitutional documents, a board resolution, and the domestic tax representative appointment form. The entity must also open a local corporate bank account, obtain access to the HomeTax e-invoice system, and, if physical goods are to be exported, obtain a Korea Customs Service exporter code through an export declaration EDI application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa; corporate classification is statutory under the Corporate Tax Act, and hybrid mismatch rules under the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs apply automatically.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for a corporation. Every business operator making taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT; the KRW 80 million simplified taxpayer turnover threshold applies only to individual entrepreneurs and does not apply to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean VAT registered businesses must issue an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice through the HomeTax platform or a certified EDI service provider no later than the day following the supply date. The NTS assigns a unique approval number and performs electronic cross-matching between issuer and recipient; this e-invoice submission to HomeTax functions as the national fiscal clearance requirement. There is no separate physical digital stamping device; the NTS e-tax invoice approval number and the mandatory real-time electronic transmission through HomeTax Open API or certified EDI constitute the anti-fraud fiscal validation mechanism. Retail cash sales must additionally be recorded through the Cash Receipt System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Articles 21 and 22 of the Value Added Tax Act for goods physically exported from Korea with a valid Korea Customs Service export declaration, goods deemed exported under statutory bonded transactions, and qualifying services supplied to non-residents or performed entirely outside Korea where the benefit is not enjoyed in Korea and the consideration is settled in foreign exchange or an approved Foreign Exchange Transactions Act method. For this private equity buyout SPV, syndicated loan arrangement, transaction structuring, and buyout advisory fees invoiced to a non-resident target, fund, or investor can qualify for 0% VAT if the recipient is a non-resident, the service is consumed offshore, and the foreign exchange is repatriated to Korea within the mandatory collection window; dividends, interest, and pure equity financing returns remain exempt financial supplies rather than zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration acceptance notice (EDI export clearance report) evidencing actual export or deemed export status
Commercial invoice and underlying export or syndicated service contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or postal dispatch certificate for goods; for services, a certificate of completion and offshore location-of-benefit analysis
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank receipt issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Overseas buyer's certificate of business existence, non-residency, or foreign tax residency certificate
Statement of foreign currency settlement and reconciliation of the export declaration to the bank remittance advice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly audit the physical export movement, invoice chain, contract authenticity, and foreign exchange repatriation. Failure to substantiate the zero-rating documentation will cause the NTS to reverse the 0% rate, assess 10% output VAT, and impose statutory additional taxes of 10% for negligent reporting or 20% for fraudulent reporting, together with tax invoice penalties for missing or invalid e-tax invoices. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the mandatory 180-day deadline triggers Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalties including fines and criminal sanctions, denial of input VAT credit related to the export, retrospective clawback of any VAT refunds previously granted, and extension of the statute of limitations for intentional evasion or disguised transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is classified as a freely convertible currency on the current account for trade in goods and services, with no mandatory surrender to the central bank for ordinary export proceeds; however, capital account transactions are subject to a notification or license regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For a private equity buyout SPV, inbound equity injections from non-resident investors require a Foreign Exchange Declaration at a designated foreign exchange bank, and the proceeds must be credited to a Foreign Investor Investment Account (외국인투자기업 전용계좌) for capital verification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is permissible once audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates are presented, but remittances exceeding certain thresholds require supporting transactional evidence to prevent disguised capital flight. The won's offshore convertibility is limited; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are traded offshore, while onshore forward contracts require underlying real demand and are restricted to hedgers with verifiable commercial exposure. Surrender of export proceeds is effectively automatic through banking channels, but exporters must report receipts within a legally prescribed period, and any retention of funds abroad beyond the limit requires prior approval. Overall, the regime is transparent and liberal compared to Asian peers, yet compliance with the Korean customs and foreign exchange reporting system remains rigorous, especially for leveraged acquisitions where debt-to-equity ratios are scrutinized under thin capitalization rules. The SPV must maintain meticulous transfer pricing and fund-flow documentation to avoid adverse administrative penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received and settled through a domestic foreign exchange bank within 6 months from the date of export declaration unless extended approval is granted by the MOEF. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into KRW for current account receipts; exporters may hold foreign currency in domestic accounts, but must file a Foreign Exchange Receipt Report within 30 days of collection. For the SPV, any incidental export trade or service income would adopt the same timeline, and failure to repatriate within the six-month window triggers a penalty and a forced conversion order.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investor Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency) plus KRW Operational Account
Investment Proceeds Managed Account (KRW) and Multi-Currency Disbursement Sweep Account
Syndicated Loan Escrow Account (USD) and Trade Settlement Current Account
Private Equity Buyout SPV Operating Account with Sub-Accounts for Facility Drawdowns

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for non-bank offshore fintech EMIs due to the Korean Financial Services Commission's regulatory stance that only licensed financial institutions may offer multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment services to resident entities. EMIs without domestic banking licenses cannot execute the mandatory Foreign Exchange Declaration or hold the Foreign Investor Investment Account required for capital verification. Even as settlement agents, they would lack clearing access to the local Korean Won interbank system and would require a commercial bank partner, negating the benefit. The legal constraint is absolute under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and any unlicensed operation would constitute illegal money transmission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors or their lawful proxy holders must appear at the designated bank branch in South Korea for the initial KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for a PE buyout SPV due to the enhanced due diligence trigger arising from the leveraged acquisition structure. For non-resident directors, a notarized proxy with a consular apostille plus a video call with the compliance officer is acceptable only for non-account-signatory roles; at least one authorised signatory with substantial debt-to-equity authority must complete the in-person branch interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) through offshore feeder funds and holding layers in a leveraged buyout SPV.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dynamic UBO chart down to every natural person holding more than 5% through the chain, with corporate registry extracts, partnership agreements, fund placement memoranda, and notarised passport copies of each significant controller. A formal source-of-wealth report attested by the GP and a licensed auditor must accompany the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual funding profile where the SPV receives equity injection and a syndicated term loan backed by target company shares, raising concern of loan-backed equity and potential shell financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copies of the original equity subscription agreement, the buyout facility term sheet from the lending syndicate, share pledge agreements, and a pro forma balance sheet proving the debt-to-equity ratio does not exceed Korean thin capitalization thresholds (currently 2:1 for related-party borrowings). Independent valuation report of the target company and a 12-month cash flow statement of the SPV must be provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious payment routing pattern where capital is to be wired from a high-risk jurisdiction or via a multi-hop chain through multiple financial centres.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete wire transfer audit trail showing the origin of funds from the committed capital account of the fund manager, a breakdown of each fund's LPs with certified source-of-funds declarations, and legal opinion letters from the originator and intermediary banks. All flows must be mapped to a signed investment agreement and reflect economic substance rather than pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential breach of Korean foreign exchange reporting because the SPV may receive proceeds exceeding USD 100,000 in a single transfer without prior declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-submitted Foreign Exchange Declaration Form (Form 2-1) to the designated foreign exchange bank, bank receipt acknowledgement, and a compliance certificate from a Korean-certified tax accountant (CPA) verifying the inward remittance matches the registered Foreign Investment Report. The SPV must also present the Certificate of Foreign Investment Registration issued by the local branch of KOTRA or the relevant ministry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital for the PE buyout SPV must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas fund account to the SPV's Foreign Investor Capital Escrow Account at a Korean Tier-1 bank. The remittance instruction must include a Foreign Exchange Declaration purpose code '921000 - Investment in stocks of a Korean corporation' for equity contributions, or '921300 - Long-term loan borrowings' for shareholder loans. On receipt, the bank verifies the declaration and issues a Negotiation Confirmation, then transfers the funds to the SPV's operating account after capital verification with the Korean Securities Depository or the local investment authority. For amounts exceeding KRW 5 billion, prior notification to the MOEF is required. No cash conversion is mandatory; the SPV may hold USD/EUR in escrow until the acquisition closing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements from the SPV to overseas sellers are executed via SWIFT MT103 for standard purchase payments, with irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) used for gross goods acquisitions. For service-based or digital content payments, MT103 with purpose code '323000 - Professional services' is preferred. Documentary collections are acceptable for low-value transactions under USD 200,000, but the SPV's internal policy defaults to L/C for any disbursement over USD 1 million to maintain an audit trail. All outbound remittances require the underlying transaction contract, invoices, and customs declarations when applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contract (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW) with a Korean bank, limited to a maturity of 1 year, requiring documented underlying exposure from the buyout deal.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) on USD/KRW permitted for non-resident counterparties, but the SPV as a resident may only use onshore deliverable forwards unless a special exemption is obtained from the MOEF.

Currency swap (cross-currency interest rate swap) between KRW and USD to hedge mismatch on the syndicated loan facility, permitted only when the loan is denominated in USD and the SPV's revenue is in KRW, with documentation proving the notional amount matches the loan principal.

Plain vanilla FX options (call/put) for downside protection on large one-shot acquisition payments, subject to the bank's real-demand rule and capped notional at 150% of the underlying transaction value.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders and approval of financial statements and shareholders' resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chusik Hoesa shareholders in general meeting (internal corporate record; no government agency filing required for non-listed company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting or to approve financial statements exposes incumbent directors to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act and may invalidate reliance on audited accounts; directors may also become personally liable for damages caused to shareholders or creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return including tax-adjusted financial statements, tax reconciliations, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) / HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% negligent non-filing additional tax on the corporate income tax amount (or 0.7% of gross revenue when no tax is due), additional taxes for underreporting ranging from 10% to 40%, statutory daily overdue interest on unpaid tax, coercive asset collection, cancellation of the business registration for chronic non-filing, administrative dissolution risk, and criminal prosecution for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return (10% local surtax on the annual corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (province or city tax office) via the NTS HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by March 31 for calendar-year corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the underpaid local income tax surtax, monthly overdue interest, enforced collection, and administrative issues affecting the business registration and tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements (mandatory only if the Chusik Hoesa meets the asset or public-interest thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the annual general meeting; the independent Korean CPA must deliver the audit report and, where applicable, file it with the Financial Supervisory Service / Securities and Futures Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual general meeting; audited financial statements must be approved within 3 months after fiscal year-end; the audit report filing with the Financial Supervisory Service, when triggered, follows the statutory post-approval window (usually within 2 weeks after the annual general meeting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to obtain a statutory audit violates the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the company may be fined, audited financial statements may be rejected, the tax return may be treated as materially defective, and directors or officers may face criminal fines or imprisonment for obstructing or falsifying the audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment status report (only if the SPV is classified as a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (by March 31 for calendar-year foreign-invested companies); major changes in foreign shareholding or foreign investment terms must be reported within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 10 million, loss of foreign-invested company tax incentives and foreign investment protection, recharacterization of the equity as ordinary financing, and enforcement sanctions by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Securities transaction tax return and share transfer record (contingent annual filing if any unlisted Chusik Hoesa shares were transferred during the fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The transferor must file the securities transaction tax return and pay tax by the last day of the month following the calendar month in which the unlisted share transfer occurs (approximately 30 days after the transfer month-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the tax due, undervaluation penalties of 10% to 30%, statutory daily late-payment interest, criminal liability for willful evasion, and possible deemed transfer-price adjustments by the NTS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is legally required for a Chusik Hoesa if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year: (1) the company is listed on a Korean securities exchange; (2) the company's total assets are at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.9 million), which is the balance-sheet asset trigger; or (3) the company is designated as a public-interest company or belongs to a financial-industry class under Article 2 of the Act, in which case asset, turnover, or headcount thresholds may be applied by sectoral regulation. For a general private nonfinancial Chusik Hoesa, there is no standalone turnover-only trigger and no standalone headcount-only trigger for statutory external audit; the general trigger is the KRW 12 billion balance-sheet test.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies, mandatory-IFRS large entities, and financial-regulatory entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or Korean SMEs Accounting Standards for non-listed private Chusik Hoesa that do not adopt K-IFRS; all audited financial statements must be prepared and presented in KRW and audited in accordance with the Korean Statements of Auditing Standards and the external audit laws of the Republic of Korea.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not require an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa to file a separate public UBO registry return with the government. The company must, however, maintain and annually verify its Register of Members so that the shareholding record is accurate as of each annual general meeting record date. For anti-money-laundering compliance, a corporate customer opening or maintaining Korean bank or investment accounts must provide current beneficial-ownership identification to the Korean financial institution, and such identification is typically refreshed on a 12-month cycle or whenever a material shareholding change occurs. For statutory tax compliance, any transfer of unlisted shares must be reported to the National Tax Service by the last day of the month following the transfer month (a 30-day reporting window), the transferor must pay securities transaction tax, and if the company is a foreign-invested entity, changes in foreign shareholding must be reported to KOTRA or the competent tax office within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditor (if any)
Register of Stock Pledges and Security Interests over Shares
Minutes Book of Shareholders' General Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings
Accounting Books and Records (journals, ledgers, vouchers, and financial statements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 3,500 per annum for a standard South Korean registered office and corporate secretarial agent; USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 per annum if local legal or tax counsel is retained for ongoing K-IFRS/K-GAAP reporting and governance support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 30,000 for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa that is required to undergo a statutory external audit due to crossing the KRW 12 billion asset threshold or a public-interest designation; nil if no statutory audit is triggered, with an optional agreed-upon procedures review costing approximately USD 2,000 - USD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate; progressive Korean corporate income tax rates of 9% / 19% / 21% / 24% applied to taxable income brackets (KRW 0-200 million / 200 million-20 billion / 20 billion-300 billion / over 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic patent box or digital-content IP box for a passive private-equity buyout SPV. A qualifying foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa may enjoy a 50% corporate income tax reduction for 3-5 years under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCA), and Free Economic Zone enterprises may enjoy tax holidays, but a leveraged buyout SPV with pure passive investment generally does not qualify. Ordinary R&D credits and employment investment tax credits are not available to a shell SPV.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 12-2: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Calculation Return) filed electronically through the HomeTax National Tax Service portal (www.hometax.go.kr), together with audited financial statements and supplementary tax reconciliation schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with semi-annual interim/preliminary tax payments for corporations whose prior-year corporate income tax liability exceeded KRW 5 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return and payment are due by March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension may be available for the return only (not full payment) if security is furnished or for foreign-company branches under the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate identification and non-resident ownership schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, corporate number, business registration number, fiscal year-end, industry code (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525910), place of incorporation, and schedule of foreign shareholders/PE fund investors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean Chusik Hoesa must be marked as a Korean domestic corporation. Attach the foreign ownership schedule and ultimate beneficial owner structure; do not file as a foreign corporation unless the SPV is a Korean permanent establishment of an overseas vehicle. If foreign shareholders exceed any reporting threshold, the return must reconcile with non-resident withholding and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from all sources, including digital content licensing, game exports, e-commerce sales, interest, management fees, dividends, and disposal gains from buyout investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Chusik Hoesa is taxed on worldwide income. Include all Korean-source revenue and allocable foreign-source revenue. Do not net intercompany flows; arm's-length gross revenue from related parties must be separately disclosed on the cross-border transaction schedule. Revenue attributable to a foreign PE shareholder must not be booked as the SPV's revenue unless a Korean taxable presence exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of sales and deductible operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs, platform fees, license costs, employee compensation, rent, buyout transaction costs, depreciation, amortization, and interest expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only ordinary and necessary expenses substantiated by contemporaneous documentation are deductible. Interest on loans from foreign controlling shareholders is subject to Korea's thin-capitalization rule (3:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial companies; 2:1 for financial companies), and the excess interest is disallowed and reclassified as deemed dividends subject to withholding. Payments to a foreign PE fund for management, consulting, or brand fees must satisfy the arm's-length standard or be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign exchange gains and losses, gains on disposal of investments, dividend income, interest income, impairment adjustments, and extraordinary buyout-related items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE buyout SPV, gains from the sale of portfolio equity and debt instruments must be classified on the tax schedules and reconciled with capital gains and foreign-source income rules. Dividends received by the SPV from non-resident portfolio companies may be taxable unless an applicable credit or treaty exemption is claimed; non-resident investors' income must not be reported here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Reconciliation of accounting income to taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses, exempt income adjustments, tax-haven transactions, thin-capitalization interest additions, valuation differences, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border related-party transactions must be adjusted to arm's length under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA). If the Korean tax authority issues a transfer pricing adjustment, corresponding adjustments must be supported. A PE SPV should not show zero operations while receiving fees from the syndicate; such a pattern invites recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax base and progressive tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all deductions, loss carryforwards, additional written-down losses, and tax-free reserves; then computed corporate income tax at the 9/19/21/24 progressive brackets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the exactly apportioned bracket tax, including the special surtax where applicable. Loss carryforwards must be evidenced by timely filed prior-year returns and, for foreign-invested structures, cannot be imported through a non-resident branch. The Korean SPV's tax base cannot be offset by its foreign parent's losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax credits, advance tax payments, and final tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits (FTC), investment tax credits, interactive tax account payments, withholding tax credits, preliminary tax payments, and final self-assessed tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is limited to the Korean corporate income tax attributable to foreign-source income (Corporate Tax Act Article 57). The SPV must not claim a credit for withholding tax paid by non-resident shareholders. If a foreign PE syndicate member received a Korean dividend, the SPV already withholding at 22% or treaty-reduced rate reports that withholding here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Cross-border transaction disclosure and transfer pricing schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of foreign related parties, transaction types, amounts, pricing methods, TP documentation status, and any unilateral/tripartite agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SPV's foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in the business year, Local File and Master File must be attached or be contemporaneously available. Country-by-Country Reporting is triggered for a Korean ultimate parent with consolidated group revenue of KRW 100 billion or more. Failure to disclose is an independent penalty and strengthens tax evasion inference.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and under-reporting are assessed under the Basic Act for National Taxes Articles 47-2 through 47-5: an additional tax of 10%-30% of the underreported/unpaid corporate tax depending on the lateness and intentionality, plus a daily overdue charge (currently 0.03% per day on unpaid tax). An intentionally false return can attract a 40% unfair-return penalty. Criminal fraud thresholds are enforced through the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 10 years or a fine up to five times the evaded tax for aggravated tax evasion, plus confiscation orders, director indictments, and exit bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate income tax withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98-5 plus 2% local income tax surtax) on dividends paid by the Korean Chusik Hoesa to non-resident shareholders, before any Double Tax Agreement reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Korean withholding agent and the National Tax Service: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (ii) a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming that the recipient is the true owner of the dividend and has no obligation to pass it on; (iii) evidence that the shareholder meets any limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose test clause in the Korea treaty; and (iv) the prescribed non-resident reduced-withholding application on HomeTax. The Korean payer may withhold at the treaty rate only if the application is filed before payment; otherwise the shareholder must pay the 22% statutory WHT and file a refund claim with the Korean tax authorities after the payment, attaching the same documentation. Tax authorities will deny relief for a conduit PE holding company that lacks business substance, employees, office, or real decision-making in the residence jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% for both cross-border interest and royalties paid to non-residents (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax). Under most Korean income tax treaties, interest is capped at 10% and industrial/commercial/cultural royalties at 10%; certain treaties provide 5% or 15% royalty caps depending on the type of asset or historic protocol. Treaty relief for royalty/interest requires TRC, beneficial ownership proof, and a description of the licensed intangible or funded debt; payments to a shell IP company in a zero-rate jurisdiction will be recharacterized as Korean-source royalty income subject to 22% and penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 (10 billion won) in aggregate transactions with foreign related parties in a business year triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation and submission with the corporate income tax return; Country-by-Country Reporting applies where the Korean ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue is KRW 100,000,000,000 (100 billion won) or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not administer a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations registration, but the National Tax Basic Act Article 14 gives tax authorities a substance-over-form power, and the LCITA and OECD BEPS anti-abuse provisions require a Chusik Hoesa SPV to demonstrate real economic activity through its core income-generating activities (CIGA): holding and financing decisions, covenant monitoring, board meetings, treasury, risk management, and employment. A passive private-equity SPV with nominal capital, no employees, no bank account substance, and no decision-making in Korea is vulnerable to a finding of corporate fiction; treaty benefits are denied, dividends are recharacterized, related-party interest and fees are disallowed, and its separate legal personality may be pierced by the courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting or understating Korean-source digital-content licensing, gaming, or e-commerce revenue in the Chusik Hoesa's corporate income tax return, creating fictitious expenses, using forged invoices from offshore PE managers, or falsifying books and records to reduce taxable income to zero and avoid Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 and Article 8, the responsible company and director face criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 10 years for habitual or aggravated evasion and fines up to five times the tax evaded; the National Tax Service will additionally assess an unfair-return penalty of 40% of the underreported tax, plus 0.03% daily late payment interest, and may reopen settled years under the 10-year fraud assessment period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: under Korean Commercial Act Articles 399/401, the director is jointly and severally liable to the company and third parties for false tax filings and fraudulent conduct. Civil asset restitution may be collected from the director's personal bank accounts, shares, and real estate; the director may be subjected to a departure ban/blacklisting under the Immigration Act for unpaid national tax delinquencies exceeding KRW 50 million, and criminal imprisonment for up to 10 years in aggravated tax-evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and Economic-Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a conduit SPV with no commercial rationale, no employees, no physical office, no independent funding or risk management, and no carrying out of core income-generating activities, solely to route gaming/digital-content dividends, royalties, or buyout gains to a foreign PE fund under a favorable DTA, or to claim tax indemnities and Luxembourg/Hong Kong/Singapore treaty benefits without beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may invoke substance-over-form under National Tax Basic Act Article 14 and the general anti-avoidance rules in LCITA Article 17 to deny DTA benefits, recharacterize the arrangement, disallow intercompany deductions, impose the 22% non-resident withholding tax on deemed dividends/royalties/interest, and assess a 40% misuse-of-law tax penalty together with interest. Criminal charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may apply if a false DTA application or forged TRC is used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign a treaty-relief package for a shell SPV can be personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties. Korean courts may disregard the separate legal personality of the Chusik Hoesa, treating the SPV's assets and income as the foreign shareholder's or parent's assets, exposing directors to civil restitution claims, attachment of personal property, prohibition on giving testimony under privilege, and criminal sanctions for aiding and abetting tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Foreign Exchange / Cross-Border Financing Infractions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PE buyout SPV receives syndicated loan proceeds, supplier credits, or equity subscription funds from non-resident funds through SWIFT without registering the foreign borrowings or capital transactions with the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; maintaining non-declared offshore bank accounts; or making cross-border payments as disguised repatriation without the required reporting and withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its enforcement decrees are subject to imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to KRW 100 million, plus confiscation of the proceeds of unlicensed foreign-exchange transactions; tax authorities may disallow deductions for unreported cross-border expenses and impose an additional 20%-40% documentary-penalty surcharge on the related corporate tax under the Basic Act for National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot hide behind the SPV: the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalizes the actual person who executes the unregistered payment, and the Korean Commercial Act makes directors jointly liable for losses caused by reckless financial handling. Directors may face travel bans, passport revocation, and exit blacklisting while investigations are pending; if the unreported remittances are tied to money laundering, anti-money-laundering laws subject directors to criminal forfeiture and imprisonment, and the director's declaration of personal bankruptcy does not discharge tax-related public law liabilities.
